The '''Gonja language''', properly called '''Ngbanya''' or '''Ngbanyito''',<ref>Mary E. Kropp Dakubu (ed.), ''The Languages of Ghana'', page 77</ref> is a [[Guang languages|North Guang language]] spoken by an estimated 230,000 people, almost all of whom are of the [[Gonja people|Gonja]] [[ethnic group]] of northern [[Ghana]].  Related to Guang languages in the south of Ghana, it is spoken by about a third of the population in the northern region. The Brong-Ahafo and Volta regions lie to the south of the Gonja-speaking area, while Dagombas, Mamprussis and Walas are to the north.<ref>''Language Guide (Gonja Version)''. Bureau of Ghana Languages, Accra, 1977-1988.</ref><ref>Kropp Dakubu, M.E. (editor), ''The Languages of Ghana''. Kegan Paul International, London, for the International African Institute. 1988.</ref> Its dialects are Gonja and Choruba.

==Alphabet==

Vowels used are: ''a,e,i,o,ɔ,u,ɛ''. Consonants include: ''ch'' {{IPA|[tʃ]}}'', ŋm, ny, gb, kp, sh'' {{IPA|[ʃ]}}.
